context: Add an ALTER TABLE branch to _statement_table (reuse the existing _ALTER_TABLE_RE), and add a regression test simulating the mixed Snowflake ledger (ALTER + OPTIMIZE on different tables) that fails today. For the truncation bound: either scope the catalog query by the ledger tables (preferred where the platform allows an IN list - both queries already filter in Python) or compute truncated only when the bound plausibly clipped relevant rows; keep the conservative refuse-on-real-truncation behavior.
description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review.

Defect (A10, latent fail-closed): _statement_table (benchbox/core/tuning/introspection.py:308-322) recognizes CREATE INDEX / OPTIMIZE / CREATE TABLE only - no ALTER branch - and the generic RecordingConnection records with table=None. #1371 made ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY the entire Snowflake tuning footprint, so a Snowflake ledger's tables set is EMPTY and the introspector's 'if tables and name not in tables' filter (snowflake_introspection.py:108) degrades to unfiltered - correct today only by accident, and it contradicts the design note's bounding promise (tuning-introspection-receipts.md:77-80). The moment any table-bearing statement (an OPTIMIZE, a CREATE INDEX) joins a Snowflake ledger, the filter activates WITHOUT the ALTER'd table, its catalog fact is filtered out, and the cluster intent verdicts ABSENT - permanent, invisible never-verify.

Nit folded in (C4c): both introspectors compute truncated from the UNFILTERED row count (clickhouse/introspection.py:80: rows fetched for the whole database; snowflake_introspection.py:101), so any database/schema with >=1000 tables sets truncated=True and permanently refuses the upgrade even when every ledger table was fetched and matched. Honest, invisible.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not build the IN list by string-interpolating raw table names
anti_patterns.instead: parameterize or strictly validate identifiers before embedding
anti_patterns.why: ledger-derived names are parsed from SQL text and must not become an injection surface

anti_patterns.dont: Do not derive ALTER targets from the statement.table metadata field alone
anti_patterns.instead: parse the table from the ALTER statement text like the other branches
anti_patterns.why: the generic RecordingConnection records table=None, so metadata-only extraction leaves the same hole

anti_patterns.dont: Do not drop the truncation refusal to 'fix' large-catalog runs
anti_patterns.instead: narrow the query or the truncation predicate so the bound measures relevant rows
anti_patterns.why: certifying against a knowingly incomplete snapshot is the over-certification failure class

preserves.behavior: A genuinely clipped catalog snapshot still refuses the upgrade (truncated => no applied_verified).
Introspection stays bounded: hard row caps remain; scoping by ledger tables may narrow reads but never widen them.
Introspectors never raise; degraded reads keep returning IntrospectedState(error=...).
RECLUSTER/maintenance ALTER classification is unchanged - only table EXTRACTION learns about ALTER, not verdict classes.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.tuning.applied_ledger import PHASE_POST_LOAD, AppliedTuningLedger; from benchbox.core.tuning.introspection import ledger_tables; led=AppliedTuningLedger(); led.record('ALTER TABLE lineitem CLUSTER BY (a)', PHASE_POST_LOAD); led.record('OPTIMIZE TABLE other', PHASE_POST_LOAD); assert ledger_tables(led) == {'lineitem','other'}, ledger_tables(led)"

work_units.evidence: Tests-first proof: ledger ALTER+OPTIMIZE returned only orders, and Snowflake mixed-ledger introspection filtered out LINEITEM entirely. Both intended regressions failed; log /tmp/item6-red.log.
work_units.notes: Add failing regression test: ledger with executed 'ALTER TABLE lineitem CLUSTER BY (a)' plus 'OPTIMIZE TABLE other' must yield ledger_tables() containing BOTH lineitem and other; introspector fake asserting the lineitem fact is not filtered out.
work_units.summary: Failing test: ledger with ALTER + OPTIMIZE on different tables must include both in ledger_tables(); introspector must not filter out the ALTER'd table

work_units.evidence: _statement_table now parses ALTER TABLE with the existing _ALTER_TABLE_RE and normalize_identifier; mixed ALTER+OPTIMIZE regressions pass.
work_units.notes: Add the ALTER TABLE branch to _statement_table using _ALTER_TABLE_RE; keep normalize_identifier semantics consistent with the other branches.
work_units.summary: Add the ALTER TABLE branch to _statement_table using _ALTER_TABLE_RE with consistent normalize_identifier semantics

work_units.evidence: ClickHouse and Snowflake retain hard LIMIT 1000 reads but compute truncated from ledger-relevant rows after normalized filtering. At-cap tests with 999 unrelated rows plus the target stay untruncated; genuinely relevant at-cap remains truncated by construction. 84 focused tests passed.
work_units.notes: Truncation bound: scope catalog reads to ledger tables where feasible (parameterized/validated) or compute truncated from relevant-row counts; unit tests for the >=cap-tables-but-all-ledger-tables-fetched case on both ClickHouse and Snowflake introspectors.
work_units.summary: Truncation: scope catalog reads to ledger tables or compute truncated from relevant rows; tests for the at-cap case on both introspectors

work_units.evidence: Receipts design note now documents ALTER-aware table extraction, hard catalog caps, relevant-row truncation, and absent fail-closed behavior when a target is clipped.
work_units.notes: Update the bounding paragraph in the receipts design note to describe the actual mechanism after the change.
work_units.summary: Update the receipts design-note bounding paragraph to the actual mechanism
